entries.english:
CCLXXXII. Emperor Karl IV confirms all privileges and liberties of the Church of Breslau. From the original in the cathedral chapter archive, C. 20 and 40, in two copies. The large imperial seal hangs from No. 29 on yellow and black silk cords; it has been lost from No. 40.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, amen. Karl IV, by the favor of divine clemency ever august Emperor of the Romans and King of Bohemia, for perpetual remembrance of the matter. If, from the inborn affection of our royal benevolence, we take pleasure in attending to the advantages and progress of all our faithful and in providing them the comforts of tranquility and peace, so that they may flourish in happy prosperity under the gracious rule of a benevolent prince, our affection is especially and zealously directed toward those whose more distinguished marks of faith and devotion have shone forth through their diligent affection and faithful service in honor of the most illustrious kings, kingdom and Crown of Bohemia.

Accordingly, considering the frequent signs of steadfast and distinguished devotion, and the indications of singular virtue and goodness with which the venerable Preczlaus, Bishop of the Church of Breslau, prince, chancellor and counsellor, and the chapter of that same church, our beloved and devoted subjects, have often honored our majesty and our father, the illustrious King Johann of Bohemia of blessed memory, and the Kingdom and Crown of Bohemia with their diligent and strenuous service, and will in future strive to honor them still more diligently and with ever more gracious service in proportion to the greater benefits of grace they have received from our majesty, we have deliberated soundly—not by mistake or rashly, but with the sound counsel of our princes, barons and nobles. By royal authority in Bohemia and with certain knowledge of our own, we approve, ratify, renew and confirm, for the said bishop and chapter of the Church of Breslau and their successors in perpetuity, in all their contents, terms, points and clauses, word for word as they are written, all the privileges and letters which they or their predecessors are known to have obtained concerning any rights, grants, liberties, immunities and indulgences from our said father, King of Bohemia, or from any dukes, counts and barons in the city and diocese of Breslau, and especially from the illustrious princes Heinrich I, Heinrich II, Heinrich III, Heinrich IV and Heinrich VI, the last dukes of Silesia and lords of Breslau, and Heinrich, Conrad and Bolko, former dukes of Glogau. These privileges shall retain their full force forever, as though their complete texts were inserted here word for word, even if law or custom would require special mention of their wording. (The editor cites Sommersberg and Lünig.)

We sincerely and in good faith promise, for ourselves, our heirs and successors as Kings of Bohemia, to maintain and preserve for the said bishop and chapter and their successors forever, inviolate and undiminished, these privileges, letters, rights, grants, liberties, immunities and indulgences. We will defend the bishop, church, chapter and secular clergy, and their persons, goods, lands, status and rights, against any kings, dukes, counts, barons, tyrants, plunderers, molesters, wrongdoers or disturbers, whatever their condition or status, and preserve them without deceit. We will do so when we learn that they or any of them have been plundered, molested or disturbed in their persons, property or rights, or injured, or when they inform us of such plunder, molestation, injury or disturbance and seek assistance from us, our heirs or successors as Kings of Bohemia.

We further promise in good faith, for ourselves, our heirs and successors as Kings of Bohemia, that at no time will we burden the bishop, church, chapter and secular clergy of the city and diocese of Breslau, or any lay people subject to them who live on church lands, with exactions, taxes, payments, demands for money, animals or provisions, services, transport duties or any other forced or extraordinary burdens, whatever name they may bear; nor will we impose lodgings or quarters in the villages and estates of the bishop, chapter, clergy and church. Instead, by royal authority in Bohemia, we grant them complete and unrestricted liberty according to the terms of their privileges. Therefore no one may violate this instrument of our approval, ratification, renewal, confirmation, promise and grant of liberty, or oppose it in any rash undertaking.

The sign of the most serene prince and lord, Lord Karl IV, the invincible and glorious Emperor of the Romans and King of Bohemia. Witnesses: the venerable Arnestus, Archbishop of the Church of Prague; Johannes, Bishop of Olomouc; Albertus, Bishop of Schwerin; and Theodricus, Bishop of Minden; the illustrious Wilhelm, Margrave of Meissen; Bolko of Świdnica; Conrad of Oleśnica; Wenceslaus and Ludowicus of Legnica; Przemyslaus of Cieszyn; Bolko of Opole; and Bolko of Falkenberg, dukes; the distinguished Burchard and Johannes, burgraves of Magdeburg; counts and nobles, including Sbinco von Hazemburg, our chief chamberlain; Jodocus and Johannes, brothers von Rosenberg; and Sdenco von Sternberg, royal court judge in Bohemia, together with many other princes, nobles and faithful subjects.

Given at Breslau under the testimony of letters bearing the seal of our imperial majesty, in the year of the Lord 1358, the eleventh indiction, on the Ides of December, in the thirteenth year of our reign and the fourth year of our empire. (The emperor’s monogram appears here.)
